title: GO: Render the first fixed Android frame from Jolt through Raylib
description:
Objective
Prove the central path: NativeActivity -> pinned Raylib entry -> Jolt export -> jolt.ffi -> Raylib -> OpenGL ES -> visible Android frame.

Why this is the go/no-go gate
No persistent loop, shared reducer, touch features, assets, audio, Raygui, or platform helpers are justified until this screenshot exists.

Existing context
Use the selected link topology, minimal binding subset, separate libjoltraylib.so, existing emulator/ADB helpers, and Raylib's frame batching rules. The Jolt function should render a fixed bounded number of frames (for example 120), not an unbounded app.

Frame content
Display Jolt + Raylib Android, Jolt/Chez/Raylib versions, API/ABI, and frame count generated by Jolt. Preserve artifacts/raylib/screenshots/001-first-frame.png. Log all runtime/thread ownership and GL facts.

Validation
From a clean checkout: pinned shell, raylib Android build, emulator start, install/run, state/log collection, ADB screenshot, image inspection, APK/ELF inspection, and crash/ANR scan. A Raylib internal screenshot may supplement but not replace ADB.

Failure policy
Acceptance is success-only. On failure, reduce the linker/FFI/runtime/render boundary, create a blocker Bead, and keep all post-gate tasks blocked. If bounded investigation concludes no-go, create a separate lower-level Raylib report task rather than closing this gate.

Scope boundary
No shared domain, touch, assets, audio, general UI, batching, or primary-host changes.
design: Keep the fixed-frame program deterministic and diagnostic. Use actual pinned APIs rather than copying the plan's pseudocode. The evidence must show ARM64 Jolt/Chez and Raylib Android backend under the API-35 translation path, not claim native ARM64 hardware.
acceptance_criteria: The documented clean commands automatically build/run the independent APK and produce an inspected ADB screenshot containing Jolt-generated runtime text from a Raylib frame; logs prove Jolt called Raylib through jolt.ffi on one native thread; APK/ELF/device evidence establishes API-35 ARM64-under-translation; no crash/ANR occurs; primary verification is unchanged.
notes: Completed 2026-08-29. Added independent :raylib-frame-android and raylib/android-frame fixture. Jolt owns a bounded 120-frame loop using only scalar jolt.ffi Raylib bindings: InitWindow, SetTargetFPS, WindowShouldClose, BeginDrawing, ClearBackground, DrawText, EndDrawing, CloseWindow. The C NativeActivity only initializes/looks up/calls/shuts down the separate Jolt library on its Raylib thread. RAY-008 clean pinned-shell command assembled/inspected the ARM64 API-35 APK, ran it on the existing x86_64 emulator, captured and visually inspected the ADB framebuffer artifact artifacts/raylib/screenshots/001-first-frame.png (1080x2400; visible Jolt/Raylib/API/ABI text and live frame 50/120), and verified both screenshot checksums. Logs show Berberis, Raylib Android backend, ANGLE/Mesa OpenGL ES Translator, jolt_lookup raylib_first_frame, result 120, and same-thread shutdown; no current-run crash/ANR. scripts/test-portable, scripts/test-android-library, primary :app:assembleDebug, and nix flake check all systems passed after the module addition. No shared reducer, input/assets/audio/Raygui/persistent-loop feature claim or primary-host change.
close_reason: Jolt-owned fixed 120-frame Raylib FFI loop renders and is visually verified on the API-35 translated ARM64 emulator.

title: Automate Android gallery interaction and lifecycle validation
description:
Objective
Provide a fail-fast gallery verification path layered onto the separate Raylib verifier.

Matrix
Build/package the ARM64 APK; verify pins and library topology; launch gallery; enter every scene; perform deterministic taps/swipes and available multi-pointer gestures; assert debug state; capture screenshots; navigate back; repeat switching; background/resume; rotate; force-stop/relaunch; scan current-run crash/ANR; preserve hashes and environment.

Constraints
Do not rely only on OCR or Android semantics, which are sparse for a rendered surface. Do not modify primary scripts/verify behavior.
design: Use live framebuffer dimensions for ADB coordinates and a machine-readable debug endpoint/log contract for assertions.
acceptance_criteria: One documented command reproduces the core gallery matrix from a clean checkout, fails on state/visual/lifecycle/crash regressions, preserves per-scene logs/screenshots/state and hashes, and leaves primary Compose/JNI verification unchanged.

title: Adapt Virtual Controls for simultaneous mobile touches
description:
Objective
Turn the pinned virtual-controls example into an adaptive gallery scene with a left D-pad and right action control that can be held simultaneously.

Adaptation
Place controls from safe live dimensions, implement generous hit areas/dead zone, map touch IDs to controls for the duration of each contact, and feed one movement/action model also usable by Linux keyboard/mouse. Depend on validated per-index touch coordinates; do not fake multitouch through mouse point zero.

Validation
Pure hit-test and touch-ID ownership tests, injected two-pointer scenarios, Android multi-touch interaction where tooling permits, single-touch degradation evidence, orientation screenshots, and Linux fallback.
design: Gate real simultaneous controls on GetTouchPosition(index) ABI evidence. Do not introduce a generic gesture framework.
acceptance_criteria: Movement and action can be independently held by two touch IDs on Android after aggregate touch ABI validation; hit targets/layout pass the size matrix; lost/reordered contacts release correctly; keyboard/mouse fallback uses the same downstream state; no Raylib structs enter scene state.

title: Adapt Flappy Bird for touch and delta time
description:
Objective
Refactor the pinned flappy-bird example into a deterministic gallery scene controlled by touch press edges, with keyboard fallback on Linux.

Adaptation
A press edge flaps; after game-over a press restarts without accidental double action. Convert gravity, velocity, scrolling, and spawning from frame constants to delta-time units; scale geometry/gaps from current dimensions; support deterministic seeded fixtures.

Validation
Pure update tests at multiple frame-step partitions, press-edge/held-touch tests, collision/scoring/restart fixtures, scripted Android taps and screenshots, Linux keyboard smoke, background/resume without a giant simulation jump.
design: Keep game state independent of polling/rendering. Clamp or otherwise explicitly handle lifecycle delta spikes.
acceptance_criteria: Equivalent elapsed-time fixtures remain within documented tolerance at 30/60/variable FPS; one held touch causes one flap; restart semantics are deterministic; Android touch gameplay, score/collision state, adaptive rendering, Linux fallback, and lifecycle resume are evidenced.

title: Render the adaptive gallery shell and navigation
description:
Objective
Render a touch-first scene chooser inside the existing Jolt-owned loop and navigate without creating Android Activities or Raylib windows.

Behavior
Show labelled cards for the six core scenes, derive card geometry and typography from current framebuffer metrics, support tap selection, an in-canvas Back target, Android Back to gallery, and Back from gallery to orderly close. Preserve selected scene/debug state.

Validation
Test portrait and landscape plus two resolutions; use ADB taps computed from live dimensions; retrieve internal screen/scene state; capture gallery and navigation screenshots; scan logcat for crash/ANR and verify one init/shutdown pair.
design: Use a single rendered surface and state machine. Minimum touch targets are metric-derived; avoid fixed 800x450 coordinates and system-gesture edges.
acceptance_criteria: The gallery opens each registered placeholder scene by touch, returns by canvas and Android Back, closes deterministically only from the gallery, remains usable in the required size/orientation matrix, exposes selected-scene state without OCR, and never reinitializes Jolt or Raylib while switching.

title: Define the gallery scene and normalized input contracts
description:
Objective
Design and implement the smallest AOT-friendly contracts that let one persistent Jolt/Raylib loop switch among gallery scenes.

Required contract
A static registry with scene id/title/init/update/draw/dispose; top-level gallery/scene state; normalized per-frame screen metrics, primary pointer press/down/release, touch count/IDs/available coordinates, gestures, Android Back, and optional keyboard fallback for Linux.

Constraints
Do not call example -main functions, reinitialize Raylib/Jolt per scene, dynamically discover namespaces, leak Vector2/pointers into portable state, or add input-gamepad. Preserve one-thread ownership.

Method and evidence
Start with REPL observations and pure transition tests. Add a tiny two-scene fake registry proving open/back/reset/dispose and input edge semantics, then compile it as a Jolt built image/shared-library source.
design: Use explicit maps/case and data, not protocols requiring runtime discovery. Separate polling from scene updates so tests can inject input snapshots.
acceptance_criteria: Pure tests and a built-image check prove deterministic registry lookup, scene init/update/draw/dispose ordering, gallery open/back transitions, press-edge semantics, live screen metrics, and no duplicate window/runtime ownership; contracts contain no gamepad or native pointer values.
notes: Completed RAY-011 gallery contract. Added explicit AOT-friendly scene descriptors/registry and top-level gallery/scene state with deterministic init-update-draw-dispose, reset, active-scene Back, and gallery-close transitions. Extended normalized snapshots with coordinate availability, gesture code, Android/keyboard Back, and Enter/Left/Right keyboard fallback; no gamepad/native pointer values or window/runtime ownership. Validation: 7 pure tests/33 assertions pass with a two-scene fake registry; pinned Android ARM64 managed-library AOT build and Gradle APK assembly pass; runtime API-35 log reports gallery-contract=1 plus gesture/keyboard state; source boundary and current-run crash/ANR checks pass. RAY-011 preserves exact commands and evidence.
close_reason: Static scene lifecycle and normalized input contracts are pure-tested, AOT-built into the ARM64 managed library, and runtime-confirmed in RAY-011 without duplicate host ownership or excluded native/gamepad state.

title: Touch-first Raylib demo gallery
description:
Objective
Build one Android NativeActivity gallery in the proven Jolt-owned Raylib loop. The gallery presents hand-picked mobile-suitable raylib-jlt examples as scenes, not separate Activities or nested example -main loops.

Included core scenes
Following Eyes, Touch Trail, Flappy Bird, Virtual Controls, raw touch/multitouch diagnostics, and gesture diagnostics. input-gamepad is explicitly excluded. Sensor-driven Ball Physics is later conditional work.

Execution boundary
One InitWindow/CloseWindow pair, one Jolt runtime, one Raylib thread, one scene registry, adaptive touch-first layout, Android Back navigation, deterministic internal state, Linux development parity where practical.

Evidence
Each leaf preserves focused tests/screenshots/logs. Final integration exercises scene switching, lifecycle, relaunch, state retrieval, and crash/ANR scans.
design: Extend the existing alternate Raylib host without changing :app. Refactor selected upstream examples into init/update/draw/dispose scene contracts and retain upstream attribution. Do not invoke their -main functions. Keep native values and frame input in the Raylib host.
acceptance_criteria: One APK exposes a touch-first gallery and all core scenes through a single stable Jolt-owned loop; navigation, adaptive layout, input normalization, Android lifecycle, debug state, Linux compile/run parity, and automated visual interaction are evidenced; input-gamepad is absent; Ball Physics remains separately conditional unless activated.

description:

Update the Raylib alternate-host source pins needed for the mobile demo gallery, revalidate the exact revisions against the existing Linux/Android host, and translate the approved gallery design into an autonomous Beads dependency graph.

Scope

Validation
Resolve revisions/licenses/API contracts; run bounded pin/compile/build regression gates; create assigned easy/medium/hard gallery tasks with explicit dependencies, acceptance evidence, and scope boundaries; inspect ready/blocked graph.
design: Reuse the existing jolt-android-lfu alternate-host graph and proven persistent loop. Add a gallery epic and focused leaves rather than broadening completed first-frame beads. Pin only revisions deliberately selected and preserve existing user changes.
acceptance_criteria: raylib/pins.edn and lock/config references agree on exact validated revisions; relevant binding namespaces compile and existing Android Raylib build gates remain valid; the Beads graph has one ordered gallery path, no input-gamepad implementation task, deferred ball-physics work, complexity assignments, and concrete reproducible acceptance criteria.

Created gallery epic jolt-android-lfu.6 with 10 core leaves plus later conditional Ball Physics; assignments use hard/medium/easy and dependencies gate generic touch diagnostics, scene shell, ABI, parity, lifecycle, and validation. input-gamepad has no task.

title: Publish the evidence-based Raylib feasibility report
description:
Objective
Synthesize Raylib experiments into docs/RAYLIB-REPORT.md and clearly assign the demonstrated R0-R6 level without changing the primary PoC's claims.

Existing context
Use docs/RAYLIB-PLAN.md's report outline/success levels, docs/RAYLIB-GOTCHAS.md, all RAY-* experiments, clean verification, measurements, screenshots, source metrics, and REPORT.md's observed/inferred/blocked language. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md may gain a clearly separate observed Raylib section only when evidence supports it.

Required conclusions
Pinned environment; proven ownership/thread/link topology; desktop/Android rendering/input/lifecycle/assets/platform call; aggregate ABI; GC/FFI measurements; REPL workflow; actual shared LOC; APK/startup/time-to-frame/memory metrics when collected; accessibility/text-input limits; comparison with Compose/JNI and GTK; upstream-suitable issues; untested audio/native ARM64/Raygui boundaries; recommended next step.

Scope boundary
Do not call translation native ARM64 hardware, compare performance from unlike conditions, close optional tasks by assertion, or merge Raylib conclusions into the primary success level.

Validation
Every claim links to reproducible evidence; source/command links resolve; docs diagnostics and link checks pass; primary REPORT/README claims remain accurate.

Escalation
If a required core experiment lacks evidence, leave it unknown and keep/report the relevant Bead rather than filling gaps with design intent.
design: A lower success level is valid. Keep proposed, observed, inferred, blocked, optional, and untested statements explicit.
acceptance_criteria: docs/RAYLIB-REPORT.md exists with reproducible evidence links and an honest R0-R6 conclusion; architecture/topology/threading, host parity, measurements, developer experience, mobile limitations, upstream opportunities, and recommended next step are covered; docs/RAYLIB-GOTCHAS.md is current; primary REPORT.md evidence boundary and scripts/verify claims remain unchanged.

title: Implement a separate clean-room Raylib verification pipeline
description:
Objective
Create a fail-fast, independently invokable Raylib verification command that reproduces supported desktop/Android evidence without changing scripts/verify semantics.

Existing context
Follow scripts/verify, scripts/screenshot, scripts/android-showcase, EXP-016, artifacts/logs/verify, and test/conformance patterns. Raylib graphics has little Android semantic UI, so combine ADB input, internal debug state, logs, and screenshots.

Required gates
raylib source/dependency check; headless namespace compilation; desktop Jolt run and real built-image/AOT smoke; Linux screenshot; Android plain-C/native/Jolt library ABI checks; APK assembly/install/launch; internal-state assertions; touch/lifecycle/assets/OpenURL scenario where supported; ADB screenshot inspection inputs; GC/FFI measurement artifact presence; scoped crash/ANR scan. Explicitly skip unsupported host-specific tiers with reasons.

Scope boundary
Do not fold Raylib into scripts/verify, delete persistent Beads data during clean checks, require Android Studio, or report skipped audio/native hardware/Raygui as passed.

Validation/evidence
Run from clean generated state with explicit pinned JOLT_SOURCE/source prerequisites. Preserve one log per tier, summary, versions, APK/ELF checks, screenshots, and exit status. Rerun primary scripts/test-portable and :app validation.

Escalation
If clean reproduction still depends on hidden checkout/cache state, fail and document the prerequisite rather than masking it.
design: Use scripts/raylib-verify and raylib-specific helper names. Make every pipeline stage fail with an unmasked exit status.
acceptance_criteria: A documented clean-state command runs all supported Raylib desktop/Android gates fail-fast, produces per-tier logs plus a summary and required screenshots/state evidence, flags current-run crash/ANR markers, reports explicit skips honestly, requires no host-installed SDK/library, leaves scripts/verify behavior unchanged, and reruns primary validation successfully.

title: Run a persistent Jolt-owned Raylib frame loop
description:
Objective
Replace the bounded first-frame loop with a normal Jolt-owned update/render loop and establish stable single-thread ownership before adding application features.

Why this task exists
A fixed frame proves reachability; R4 requires Jolt to remain on the Raylib thread while polling input, rendering, allocating bounded state, handling focus, and closing normally.

Existing context
Use the first-frame source and topology. Raylib's Android PollInputEvents blocks while unfocused unless FLAG_WINDOW_ALWAYS_RUN, and its backend handles TERM_WINDOW/context rebind. Jolt remains inside one exported call for the loop; do not re-enter it from C each frame.

Expected approach
Start low-allocation. Add a debug log/state endpoint with frame, FPS/frame time, thread, focus/lifecycle marker, and clean shutdown state. Run 30 seconds, 5 minutes, and 15 minutes; background/resume once and relaunch.

Scope boundary
No shared reducer, assets/audio, performance batching, nREPL, or Raygui. Do not optimize before measuring.

Validation/evidence
RAY-006 logs, ADB/internal state, screenshots, frame-time summary, memory snapshots, lifecycle transitions, close/relaunch, no crash/ANR, and automated bounded mode.

Escalation
If loop stability requires changing runtime ownership or another thread entering Jolt, stop and create an architecture blocker.
design: Preserve tail-call/stack and allocation observations. Keep diagnostics removable/debug-only and retrievable without OCR.
acceptance_criteria: Jolt owns the normal Raylib loop for 15 minutes under the tested emulator, all Jolt/Raylib calls remain on the recorded native thread, frame/memory diagnostics are retrievable, background/resume and clean close/relaunch are observed, and no stack growth/crash/ANR occurs; any bounded instability is reduced and classified.
notes: Completed 2026-08-30. Added independent raylib/android-loop fixture, :raylib-loop-android module, pinned cross-build/package scripts, and RAY-009 lifecycle evidence. Jolt owns one bounded 905-second normal loop after a single C entry: InitWindow, WindowShouldClose, GetFrameTime, BeginDrawing/ClearBackground/DrawText/EndDrawing, and CloseWindow all execute within the Jolt export on the recorded NativeActivity thread. Clean emulator run captured 30s, post-lock/unlock resume, 5m, and 15m ADB screenshots plus identify, dumpsys meminfo, gfxinfo, PID, and full logcat artifacts. Visual diagnostics show frame/time/FPS; final frame 27003 at 902513 ms and final export returned 27078 frames, then same-thread shutdown. Native heap stayed about 8.2 MB across milestones. Lifecycle log shows TERM_WINDOW/INIT_WINDOW on background/resume. A fresh relaunch initialized the loop and remained alive; no current-run Fatal signal, FATAL EXCEPTION, or ANR. Validation: initial full 15-minute run passed through final close; corrected relaunch assertion verified against captured evidence; portable tests, primary Android ABI gate, primary :app assembleDebug, and flake checks passed. A TraceLog varargs diagnostic was reduced and removed after it terminated the translated process; stable on-screen/ADB diagnostics remain. Translation only; no shared reducer/assets/audio/Raygui/nREPL/batching.
close_reason: Jolt-owned Raylib loop survives 15-minute translated run, lifecycle resume, clean close, and relaunch with diagnostics and no crash/ANR.

title: Establish a viable Jolt-to-Raylib symbol topology
description:
Objective
Prove and select one native-library topology that lets the embedded Jolt library resolve and call Raylib symbols, testing preferred topology A first.

Preferred experiment
Topology A keeps Raylib statically linked into libmain.so and Jolt/Chez in libjoltraylib.so. From Jolt, use process-symbol lookup to call first a trivial bootstrap C symbol and then one safe Raylib function. Inspect visibility/export-dynamic behavior and confirm only one Raylib instance exists.

Existing context
Jolt native interop documents :process true/process lookup. The minimal binding task supplies exact names. Android Jolt currently loads separately with dlopen; Raylib's Android static build/link flags include NativeActivity and fopen wrapping requirements.

Conditional fallback rule
Do not create topology B/C work preemptively. If A fails after reduction, preserve RAY-004 and create a separate Topology B (packaged libraylib.so) Bead as a blocker of this decision. Create Topology C (Raylib archive linked into Jolt library) only if B also exposes a structural failure. This decision closes only when one viable topology has positive evidence; an irreducible no-go leaves first-frame work blocked and triggers a report-only Bead.

Scope boundary
Resolve/call one trivial C symbol and one Raylib symbol only. Do not draw a frame, bind broad APIs, or patch Jolt/Raylib before reducing visibility/loading facts.

Validation/evidence
ELF dynamic symbols, DT_NEEDED/RUNPATH, APK lib layout, dlopen/dlsym/Jolt lookup logs, one Raylib instance, thread ID, and clean relaunch.

## Decision
Record the topology selected after positive evidence; this field is intentionally unresolved until the experiment runs.

## Rationale
Prefer the topology with one Raylib instance and the smallest proven Android/Jolt loading surface.

## Alternatives Considered
A: Raylib static in libmain.so with process lookup (test first). B: packaged libraylib.so (activate only if A fails). C: Raylib archive inside the Jolt library (activate only if A and B fail).
design: Prefer A. Treat link topology as an experimental decision, not a build refactor. A failed topology is not evidence Jolt cannot call Raylib if another topology remains untested.
acceptance_criteria: One topology is selected with a minimal Android experiment proving same-thread Jolt process/native lookup and successful invocation of a trivial bootstrap symbol plus one pinned Raylib symbol; binary/APK/linker evidence explains why it works; failed alternatives, if any, are reduced; downstream first-frame work remains blocked until positive evidence exists.
notes: Completed 2026-08-29. Topology A selected and proven in RAY-007. A separate API-35 arm64-v8a NativeActivity statically links pinned Raylib into libmain.so with --export-dynamic; Jolt/Chez remains in distinct libjoltraylib-topology.so with no Raylib DT_NEEDED. The Jolt fixture uses an optional scoped libmain.so native candidate because the pure :process true form failed after direct C dlsym succeeded (reduced in RAY-007 evidence). Jolt ffi resolves GetScreenWidth against the already-loaded libmain image and returns the safe pre-window value 0. APK inspections show ANativeActivity_onCreate, android_main, and GetScreenWidth in libmain; only platform DT_NEEDED libraries; APK has exactly libmain and libjoltraylib-topology. The reproducible RAY-007 command ran two translated ARM64 launches, each logged direct process dlsym, Jolt init, jolt_lookup, Raylib result 0, shutdown, and completion on one owner thread (20181 then 20235), with no current-run crash/ANR. No fallback topology B/C is needed; drawing and first-frame work remain downstream.
close_reason: Topology A works: separate Jolt library resolves pinned static Raylib in libmain and calls GetScreenWidth on the same translated NativeActivity thread across relaunches.

title: Bootstrap Jolt on Raylib's NativeActivity thread
description:
Objective
From the plain Raylib NativeActivity application entry, initialize the Raylib-host Jolt library, resolve/call the no-op export, return, and shut down on the same native thread.

Why this task exists
This is the R2 gate and tests the opposite ownership model from Kotlin JoltRuntime: Raylib/native_app_glue owns the thread and C enters Jolt once.

Existing context
The pinned Raylib source's android_main/application-main seam was recorded by the pin task. Jolt native interop requires init, lookup, every export, and shutdown on one OS thread. EXP-005/006 prove the requirement in the primary host but do not prove NativeActivity lifecycle/global behavior.

Smallest experiment
Keep C bootstrap tiny; log Android UI/main thread if obtainable, native_app_glue/application thread, Jolt init, export, return, and shutdown IDs. The Jolt function should only emit a bounded log/return marker.

Scope boundary
No HandlerThread/Kotlin ownership, Raylib calls from Jolt, frame loop, shared reducer, debug server, or alternate thread activation.

Validation/evidence
Package/run/relaunch under translation; assert export lookup/call and clean shutdown; inspect logcat/crash markers; preserve RAY-003 commands and exact thread IDs.

Escalation
On init/lifecycle failure, reduce Jolt versus NativeActivity before CFFI. Do not call Jolt from another thread or close this gate on a workaround.
design: Use the selected pinned Raylib entry seam, not the plan's stale conceptual function name. Fail loudly on dlopen/dlsym/init/lookup errors and leave failed initialization terminal.
acceptance_criteria: The independent APK initializes Jolt, resolves and executes the no-op export, returns and shuts down with all Jolt entry on one recorded NativeActivity/native-app-glue thread; force-stop/relaunch repeats deterministically; no HandlerThread or primary-host code is reused.
notes: Completed 2026-08-29. Added an independent :raylib-jolt-android API-35 ARM64 NativeActivity module with static pinned Raylib in libmain.so and separately packaged libjoltraylib.so. The C main follows the pinned android_main -> main(int,char**) seam, dlopens the Jolt library, initializes it, resolves/calls raylib_host_noop, shuts it down, and logs every operation with Linux thread IDs. RAY-006 commands build/package/inspect the APK and run it twice on the existing API-35 x86_64 emulator. Evidence reports x86_64 with arm64-v8a translation, Berberis, successful NativeActivity load, dlopen, init, jolt_lookup, result 7, shutdown, and completion; both runs use one consistent owner thread (15522, then 15561) and have no current-run crash/ANR. The unchanged primary library ABI gate and :app:assembleDebug also pass. No HandlerThread, primary host code, Raylib call from Jolt, frame loop, or feature work was added.
close_reason: Independent Raylib NativeActivity initializes, resolves, calls, and shuts down the no-op Jolt library on one translated native thread across relaunches.

title: Build a no-op Jolt library for the Raylib Android host
description:
Objective
Produce a separate Android ARM64 Jolt/Chez managed library for the Raylib host with one no-argument exported entry that returns without calling Raylib.

Why this task exists
This reuses the proven cross-target machinery while keeping Jolt library construction separate from NativeActivity bootstrap and CFFI symbol lookup.

Existing context
scripts/jolt-android-library-build, experiments/EXP-004, native/chez/android-arm64, and Jolt Beads d06.1/d06.2 establish upstream cross --library support, Android PIC/Bionic flags, jolt_library_init/lookup/shutdown, and a temporary source worktree. The current script is hard-coded to the primary poc.native fixture and adds an experiment-only compaction hook.

Scope boundary
Do not alter libjoltpoc.so, add Raylib static libraries, use the primary reducer, call Raylib, or require the EXP-005 compaction patch unless a Raylib-specific experiment proves it necessary.

Expected approach
Create a separate Raylib Jolt fixture and build command/output (for example libjoltraylib.so). Reuse or narrowly extract identical target-pack preparation; keep source revision checks and Bionic link flags explicit.

Validation/evidence
file/readelf/nm/DT_NEEDED, required Jolt ABI symbols, jolt_lookup table entry, clean rebuild, and unchanged primary Android library/APK validation.

Escalation
If reuse requires redesigning the primary build or patching upstream Jolt, preserve a reduced RAY-* build failure and create a focused blocker.
design: This task proves AOT/cross-library construction only. Do not package/call it from NativeActivity yet.
acceptance_criteria: A clean pinned-shell command builds a distinct API-35 AArch64 Jolt library with jolt_library_init, jolt_lookup, jolt_library_shutdown, and one resolvable no-op Raylib-host export; Bionic dependencies are inspected; primary libjoltpoc.so/build commands remain unchanged.
notes: Completed 2026-08-29. Added isolated raylib/android-jolt fixture exporting only raylib_host_noop() => 7, scripts/raylib-jolt-android-library-build, and RAY-005 evidence. The clean pinned Jolt ae5c5a6d + Chez v10.4.1 + NDK r29/API-35 tarm64le command builds distinct native/jolt/android-arm64/arm64-v8a/libjoltraylib.so. ELF evidence: AArch64, Android 35, DT_NEEDED only libm.so/libdl.so/libc.so; nm exports jolt_library_init, jolt_lookup, jolt_library_shutdown. A host-built copy resolves raylib_host_noop through jolt_lookup, calls it, and shuts down cleanly. The command performs two clean Android builds, then runs unchanged scripts/test-android-library and :app:assembleDebug successfully. No Raylib archive, primary reducer, primary script, or NativeActivity packaging/call participates. Clean rebuilds succeed but bytes differ because Jolt embeds temporary flat-image paths; this is recorded rather than hidden.
close_reason: Distinct API-35 AArch64 no-op Raylib-host Jolt library built and ABI/lookup/primary-gate evidence recorded.

title: Isolate the minimal reusable Jolt Raylib binding subset
description:
Objective
Establish the smallest binding surface needed for first Android frame while reusing raylib-jlt substantially unchanged.

Why this task exists
The pinned raylib-jlt dependency declares desktop dynamic libraries and a large example namespace. The Android library needs only InitWindow, WindowShouldClose, BeginDrawing, ClearBackground, DrawText, EndDrawing, CloseWindow, GetScreenWidth/Height, and test helpers, with an Android-compatible native declaration/link strategy.

Existing context
Use the pinned upstream net.b12n.raylib-jlt.raylib source and desktop baseline. Current Jolt native interop supports :process true and literal [:by-value [:struct ...]] layouts; raylib-jlt also documents packed Color and older architecture-specific pointer workarounds. Trust neither workaround on Android AArch64 without evidence.

Scope boundary
Do not fork/rename the public API, copy the full example suite, bind all Raylib, or decide Android link topology here. Separate reusable binding source from host native-library declaration with the smallest adapter only if dependency composition requires it.

Expected approach

title: Validate the Linux Raylib nREPL development loop

Validation/evidence

title: Measure Jolt-to-Raylib FFI call volume

Objective

Experiment

Validation/evidence
Warmup/multiple runs, raw timing, frame distributions, device/emulator/version facts, call counts, scene cost, and RAY-016 report.

Escalation
If direct calls materially violate the measured frame budget, create a separate conditional batching Bead with the threshold and expected comparison. If not, record that batching is unjustified and create nothing.

acceptance_criteria: Reproducible measurements separate CFFI from rendering for 100/1k/10k calls at 30/60 FPS, include raw and summarized data, state tested translation limitations, and make an evidence-based no-batching or activate-batching decision without implementing batching here.

title: Stress Jolt GC and lifecycle during Raylib rendering
description:
Objective
Measure stability and frame-time effects for low-allocation, idiomatic persistent-state, and deliberate-allocation Jolt workloads inside the Android Raylib frame loop.

Why this task exists
The primary JNI stress evidence does not cover hundreds/thousands of CFFI calls per second, OpenGL rendering, NativeActivity surface changes, or frame deadlines.

Workloads

Metrics/evidence
FPS/frame-time distribution and spikes, native/Jolt heap proxies, process memory, GC logs if observable, crashes, ANRs, surface recovery, exact versions, and repeatability. Preserve RAY-017.

Scope boundary
Research stability, not competitive benchmarking or optimization. Do not adopt mutable redesign or batching based on intuition.

Escalation
A crash or material frame stall must be reduced to allocation, GC, CFFI, lifecycle, or GPU before proposing architecture changes.
design: Use comparable fixed scenes and collect raw data plus summary. Keep primary Compose comparisons out unless collected under the same conditions.
acceptance_criteria: All three workloads have reproducible 30s/5m/15m results with frame/memory/lifecycle evidence; stable cases and failures/stalls are honestly classified; a reduced reproduction exists for any crash/ANR; no speculative optimization is introduced.

title: Probe an Android SDK action through upstream Raylib
description:
Objective
Prove or bound one platform-neutral Raylib call that reaches the Android SDK from Jolt, initially OpenURL.

Why this task exists
This tests the distinct path Jolt -> jolt.ffi -> Raylib C API -> Raylib Android JNI -> Android, and allows an evidence-based comparison with the primary EDN-effect/Kotlin adapter.

Existing context
src/shared/poc/reducer.cljc already emits :platform/open-uri. The pinned Raylib Android source implements OpenURL with JNI and restricts schemes/quotes. Use the independent host and shared reducer adapter; no primary Kotlin code.

Validation
Trigger from Jolt-owned state, verify the exact intent/browser/chooser or deterministic emulator limitation, return/resume rendering, thread/JNI logs, and malformed URL rejection. Preserve RAY-012.

Scope boundary
One upstream Raylib API only. No generic Android SDK binding, RayMob import, direct Java reflection layer, or claim that all Android APIs are reachable.

Escalation
If OpenURL fails in plain C too, classify as RAYLIB_ANDROID; if only Jolt fails, reduce JOLT_FFI/linking separately.
design: A platform limitation is an acceptable result if plain-C and Jolt paths are separated and exact evidence is preserved.
acceptance_criteria: A Jolt event invokes pinned Raylib OpenURL on Android and the resulting intent/return behavior is evidenced, or a minimal plain-C-versus-Jolt reproduction identifies the blocking layer; unsafe URL cases are rejected; the report has enough evidence to compare this path with the primary Kotlin effect adapter.

title: Load packaged assets and writable state through the Raylib host
description:
Objective
Prove logical asset loading and writable-state boundaries on Android and Linux from Jolt through the pinned Raylib host.

Existing context
Pinned Raylib Android wraps fopen only when the final link carries -Wl,--wrap=fopen; static/archive consumers must propagate that flag. Its backend sets internalDataPath for storage. Current raylib-jlt avoids some LoadTexture APIs because aggregate returns were historically difficult; use the completed ABI evidence rather than assuming that limitation remains.

Expected approach

title: Verify Raylib CFFI aggregate ABI on Android AArch64
description:
Objective
Establish representative Raylib struct-by-value argument/return behavior for current Jolt on Android AArch64 and compare it with x86_64 Linux.

Why this task exists
Raylib uses Color, Vector2/3, Rectangle, Camera2D/3D, Texture2D and other aggregates. The pinned raylib-jlt docs include packed-Color and architecture-specific pointer workarounds, while current Jolt documents literal [:by-value [:struct ...]] support including aggregate returns. Apple AArch64 observations do not prove Android AArch64 or x86_64.

Method
For each representative signature inspect the pinned C declaration and exact Jolt layout, assert C sizeof/offsets, run numerical or visual tests on desktop and Android, and distinguish by-value arguments from returns. Include Color, Vector2, Vector3, Rectangle, Camera2D, Camera3D, and Texture2D or the smallest equivalent return.

Scope boundary
Do not bind the whole API or preserve an unsafe trick merely because it rendered once. Use a tiny C shim only when direct ABI support is demonstrably unavailable and the needed API justifies it.

Validation/evidence
Built-image plus Android shared-library tests, C oracle values, readelf/ABI, screenshots where numerical output is insufficient, and one minimal reproduction per discrepancy.

Escalation
Create upstream-specific Beads for JOLT_FFI or RAYLIB_JLT_BINDING failures; do not fold a compiler/ABI redesign into an easy adapter task.
design: Prefer current documented Jolt layouts over stale workarounds, then verify. Record which existing raylib-jlt declarations are reusable unchanged and which are architecture-specific.
acceptance_criteria: A preserved matrix gives source declarations, Jolt layouts, sizes/offsets, desktop and Android results for representative aggregates; direct calls are visually/numerically correct or failures are reduced and classified with the responsible layer; first-frame scalar bindings remain stable.

title: Validate NativeActivity lifecycle and Jolt/Raylib reset behavior
description:
Objective
Characterize focus, surface, activity, and process lifecycle in the Raylib ownership model, including deterministic reset/relaunch behavior.

Why this task exists

Smallest experiment
Instrument public Raylib state and thread IDs first. Exercise launch, home/background, resume, rotate/configure, destroy/activity recreation, force-stop/process relaunch, and orderly close. Check Raylib and Chez/Jolt global init/shutdown, double-init/double-shutdown rejection, surface/context restoration, and resources.

Fallback rule
If an important lifecycle event is not exposed publicly, add only a tiny normalized C hook after proving the gap; send data such as :platform/focus-lost, never android_app* into portable code.

Validation/evidence
ADB lifecycle commands, logs with APP_CMD/state/thread/frame, screenshots after resume, process IDs, crash/ANR scan, and a reduced RAY-010 report.

Escalation
A runtime/global reset failure is hard architecture work; do not hide it with process-only testing or switch host models.
design: Keep lifecycle hooks host-specific and preserve the one Jolt thread. A classified lifecycle limitation is an acceptable research result and should flow into the final success level.
acceptance_criteria: The lifecycle matrix records observed focus/surface/activity/process transitions, Jolt/Raylib initialization and shutdown counts, thread IDs, context/resource behavior, and post-resume rendering; double-entry misuse fails deterministically; any unsupported event or reset failure is reduced and classified.

title: Decide whether to activate Raygui R7 stretch work

Scope
Do not implement Raygui in this decision and never make it a blocker for core Raylib conclusions.

## Decision
Record GO or NO-GO after reviewing the completed core report; this remains unresolved until then.

## Rationale
R7 is justified only when R6 evidence shows the immediate-mode UI experiment would answer a remaining project question.

## Alternatives Considered

design: This is a conditional stretch activation decision, not an autonomous implementation task. Technical rendering and acceptable Android UX must remain separate questions.
acceptance_criteria: A documented GO/NO-GO references the completed core evidence; GO creates a small separate dependency graph under the Raygui epic, while NO-GO creates no speculative implementation tasks; core Raylib status is unaffected.
